pages.text: "I'll put them on! Me!" Nils the little bear gripped his blue boots. Grandpa Bruno smiled. "Try by yourself." The yard was all mud. Nils wanted to splash.
Standing, he shoved a foot into a boot. His heel caught halfway. Hopping on one foot, he fell into the mud. One boot still hung half on. "I want to splash! Ooh!"
Nils flung the boot off into mud farther away. "I can't even put on boots..." He bowed his head, nose stinging. However he pulled, his heel wouldn't go in.
Grandpa sat him on a stump. "Hard while standing. A boot is a little burrow for a foot." His broad palm spread the boot opening round.
"Going into a burrow, sing this. Foot in, boot on!" Grandpa shook the boot. "Like a burrow?" Nils's ears perked. The difficult boot was now a burrow he wanted to enter.
First! On the stump, Nils held the boot in both paws and slipped his toes in. "Foot in!" Toes entered the burrow. Not hard now, just a burrow.
Second! With his heel caught, Nils stayed seated and stamped it down. Thump, thump! The heel slid to the bottom. "Boot on!" He and Grandpa called together, "Foot in, boot on!"
The other boot too. Foot in, thump, thump, boot on! Both by himself! Nils hopped from the stump into mud. Splash! Splash!
Three steps. "One, sit! Two, foot in! Three, heel thump, thump, boot on!" Next day, Nils put them on alone. Both paws high! "Foot in, boot on!"
Grandpa held Nils and rubbed cheeks. "Boots on by yourself too!" A boot isn't difficult; it is a little burrow for a foot. In Grandpa's arms, Nils called, "Foot in, boot on! Alone tomorrow too!"
